name: buckling-plate-uniaxial-hex20
reference: Benchmark B5b: a simply supported square plate under uniaxial compression, E = 210 GPa, nu = 0.3, 1000 x 1000 x 10 mm. sigma_cr = k pi^2 D / (b^2 t) with k = 4 for a square plate compressed on one pair of edges (Timoshenko & Gere, Theory of Elastic Stability, 2nd ed., section 9.2) and D = E t^3 / (12 (1 - nu^2)) = 19230.77 N m: sigma_cr = 75.920 MPa, so lambda = 75.920 against the 1 MPa reference pressure. Gated at 3 %, which is what a single quadratic element through a 10 mm thickness earns. Modelled as one quarter, 500 x 500 x 10 mm of hex20: xmin and ymin are the real plate edges (simply supported, uz = 0, in-plane free), xmax and ymax are the centrelines of the sin(pi x / a) sin(pi y / b) fundamental mode, where ux and uy are respectively zero. The unloaded edge is free in-plane, so the pre-buckling state is uniaxial: sigma_yy = 0, which is what the k = 4 value belongs to.

checks.note: sigma_cr = 4 pi^2 D / (b^2 t) over the 1 MPa reference stress
the pre-buckling static state balances its applied load
